question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x=1+2{sinh}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(1-16{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[1-16\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1)]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(9-8\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(9x-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =[9\operatorname{ln}⁡2-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡2)]-[9\cdot 0-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡0] \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2-4\cdot \frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{2} \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2({2}^{2}-{2}^{-2}) \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{15}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
